scope: lifecycle:data-retention-sweep (apps/web/lib/operate/retention/policies.ts — new discoveryRun purge policy, 30d, cascades DiscoveredItem + DiscoveredRelationship); apps/web/lib/queue/functions/contributor-inventory-sync.ts + apps/web/lib/contributor-change-lanes/read-model.ts — ContributorInventorySnapshot write-on-change with snapshotRunId pointer
rationale: BI-BFFB9211 (EP-A33A5C61 slice 3). Two writers re-inserted every observation on every run: DiscoveredItem held 280,053 rows for 335 distinct keys across 3,784 DiscoveryRuns in 16 days with no retention at all (the cascade parent, DiscoveryRun, was never enrolled), and ContributorInventorySnapshot held 185,682 rows for 1,139 distinct keys, 99% byte-identical to the previous 10-minute run. This change (a) enrols DiscoveryRun in the existing sweep at 30 days, excluding in-flight runs and any run that is the last confirming run for an InventoryEntity or InventoryRelationship, so the raw observation log is bounded while the deduplicated truth (InventoryEntity/InventoryRelationship with lastSeenAt) and the reviewable derivatives (identityResolutionLog, fingerprint observations, triage decisions) are untouched; and (b) makes the contributor-inventory sync write snapshot rows only when the source's content digest differs from the previous successful run, recording a snapshotRunId pointer that the read model and the 7-day prune preserve-set follow. Neither table holds personal data beyond what the source systems already publish (branch names, PR metadata, network device identifiers). The data-impact gate requires per-run disposition EVIDENCE for a destructive path; that runtime artifact (BI-F0F3887F, EP-A33A5C61 slice 5) does not yet exist. This exception covers the disposition-evidence requirement only; the legal-hold exclusion is applied in code to every purge WHERE, unchanged by this PR (no discovery model carries a legalHold column).
compensatingControl: The new policy runs inside the existing sweep: after the 03:00 backups, behind the ScheduledJob kill switch, dry-run capable, batched at 1,000 rows with a 100,000-row per-policy cap, reported per label in the rolling run summary. The extraWhere is asserted by retention.test.ts (status != running, confirmedEntities none, confirmedRelations none). Write-on-change never loses an observation: a run that skips writing records the run id that holds the representation, the read model follows that pointer (tested in read-model.test.ts), and the prune preserves both the latest successful run and the run it points at (tested in contributor-inventory-sync.test.ts). A provider 304 response, which previously produced an empty 'latest successful' run and a blank lane page, now resolves to the prior representation.
